What makes bears so amazing?

Big and strong, the bear is an omnivore that eats fish, honey, and berries alike. It also has the fascinating habit of sleeping in a den through the cold winter.

We've gathered all sorts of stories about bears here — bear facts, bear hibernation, bear ecology, and more.

content.alt: Bear - Nature and science facts about bears
content.text:
Nature and science facts about bears

Bears are omnivores that eat both meat and plants, and they love fish, honey, and berries. With their keen sense of smell they can pick up the scent of food far away, and their big, sturdy claws let them dig the ground or climb trees. In winter, when food is scarce, they hibernate in a den to save energy, and mother bears usually give birth to their cubs in the winter den and lovingly raise them until spring.

Great points to observe together

Point out things like being omnivorous (fish, honey, berries), the keen sense of smell and claws, hibernation, and mother-and-cub bonds. It's fun to talk together about "Why do bears sleep in winter?"

content.alt: Bear - Parent guide — how to spark curiosity
content.text:
Parent guide — how to spark curiosity

Talk about how bears "get through the foodless winter by sleeping (hibernation)," and compare them with other hibernating animals like frogs and squirrels. It's also fascinating to point out that a bear's sense of smell is far better than a person's.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Q. Why do bears hibernate?
A. In winter food is scarce, so they sleep in a den to save energy.

Q. What do bears eat?
A. They are omnivores that eat both meat and plants. They especially enjoy fish, honey, and berries.

Q. How can we observe them at home?
A. Comparing bears with other hibernating animals and talking about how they "get through winter by sleeping" works well.
